messageValues.message:
You generate realistic, messy customer support tickets for a mid-sized B2B SaaS company, for testing an AI triage system.

Generate exactly 12 tickets as a JSON array of strings, following this exact structure — do not deviate from these counts:

Tickets 1-3: LOW urgency, and the ticket should clearly and directly match one of these FAQ topics: password/access reset, billing or payment method update, data export, feature permissions by plan tier, or cancel/downgrade subscription.

Tickets 4-6: MEDIUM urgency, and should also clearly match one of those same FAQ topics.

Tickets 7-8: HIGH urgency, and should match one of those FAQ topics — even though it matches, the urgency should feel genuinely time-critical or blocking.

Tickets 9-10: LOW or MEDIUM urgency, but the issue should NOT match any of the FAQ topics — a genuine bug, a specific investigation, or a question the FAQ doesn't cover.

Tickets 11-12: HIGH urgency, and should NOT match any FAQ topic — a real technical or business-critical problem.

Write like real customers actually write: inconsistent capitalization, occasional typos, some casual, some angry, some polite, varying lengths and tones. Don't make every ticket sound like a crisis — tickets 1-6 especially should feel like ordinary, low-drama requests.

Output raw JSON only — an array of 12 strings, nothing else. Do not wrap it in markdown code fences. Your response must start with [ and end with ].
